albums.title: Iowa
albums.description: A quiet collection of homegrown moments — this is the State I grew up in, for the most part. I came to Iowa from New Mexico. Technically, a strange year in Nebraska but I act like that year never existed. When you hear a common question from one of the best movies ever made, 'Is this heaven?' 'No, it's Iowa' I always thought, 'A slice of heaven, possibly.' It truly was where my life finally calmed down, I got to sleep in my own bed, in my own room, in a house my dad owned. I had friends that I grew up with, year after year we rode bikes and we played basketball, tennis, soccer, softball...the games never ended. I felt like it was a dream come true where kids got to be kids and scary nights stopped being so scary.

photos.caption: Fell in love on this street. 'My heart was captured.'
On this same street, my heart broke. For the next four years I went on the run...it was one of my most formative experiences.
Visiting Cedar Rapids and my daughter, 'Mom, I know a spot' and takes me to the most beautiful willow tree.
Palisades - Kepler State Park

I bought my dream house in 2019 and walked to Prairie Fishery almost every day. I worked my a$$ off for this accomplishment. I could hardly believe I did it. I remember sitting in the finished basement, just got the keys, and crying. Tears of absolute happiness. Then love happened, or I should say, didn't happen. Sold my dream house, left family, friends, my entire life to go on the run. Looking back, God saw around the corners I was blinded too. As for me, I ran. Tail tucked and I wanted to hide, possibly forever.
Lightening storm in Cedar Rapids. That is infact lightening going across the sky. It was lighting the sky up almost every 20 seconds. It felt like fireworks from heaven.
On a walk with my dad talking about life. Some of my most meaningful conversations happened in these quiet moments.
I wanted to show my dad this magical wooden path that hovered over a pond that was surrounded by trees. Sadly, all the trees were dead and the pond dried up.
Upside down or rightside up?
Discovered that my dad had never explored these trails and I was showing him something new! After living in an area for 20+ years, this has to be almost a miracle
My dad 'Kris, want to see a cool split rock?' Into Marion we drove.
The sunset gleaming off the pond.
The split rock! Right off Hwy 13
My daughter and her girlfriend were in good spirits for a couple photoshoot! So much fun!
Doesn't matter if you are black or white - M. Jackson
Love covers a multitude of sins - 1 Peter 4:8
Now that's a welcome sign! It's never goodbye, it's always see you later
My dad planted this natural privacy fence and now it carefully collects each snow flake like precious pieces of time.
Lake MacBride - on a blanky with my baby

This trail and I are close companions. Over the years, it's seen me smiling from ear to ear and it's seen me crying my eyes out. When I made Varsity Tennis, I walked this trail and could not stop smiling. I had never fought so viciously for something I wanted before. I battled for my spot and I won. I remember crying my eyes out until the tears stopped forming after my High School boyfriend of four years dumbed me. He wanted to explore other options and I thought we were going to marry. Ha Ha. Oh boy.

albums.title: Nature
albums.description: Soft light, open air, and the quiet poetry of the natural world — a space to breathe. This is where I do 'church'. People speak of God sometimes and I wonder if we are still talking about Jesus Christ or if they have a different God. Sometimes I feel like church lost it's way and I feel like a stranger sitting in God's home. I have found that nature is where I feel closest to God. The beauty, the stillness, the grandeur of it all reminds me of the Creator and the love He has for us. When I am in nature, I feel a sense of awe and wonder that is hard to put into words. It's a reminder that there is something bigger than us at work in this world and that we are a part of something much greater than ourselves.

photos.caption: Bryce Canyon - heading to the Grand Canyon to camp with my Aunt.
Pulled over and hiked around with my aunts two fur babies.

Remember when I mentioned going on the run? I spent almost every free weekend taking a road trip. This weekend gateway was spent in a crappy motel room that had the worst wall decor - but I learned a lot about the metabolic benefits to drinking a glass of water starting at 7:00 am...don't ask.
Seaside, CA and a drive down Hwy 101.
Moving to Las Vegas has it's benefits. In about 4 hours in any direction I can be at some of the most epic places. Here...the Grand Canyon. Seeing it for the first time.
Seeing is believing and now I see why so many folks love the Grand Canyon.
Do you seee all the little people? Hardly, it's the Grand Canyon!
Took my aunt all the way back home, Saint Paul, MN. A city that will forever be close to my heart.

Sedona, AZ - where I accidently locked the keys in the RV while it was running and the dogs were inside. At least the AC was on AND they got to eat our lunch that remained on the counter. I STRESSED and they ate and napped like they were on vacation! When I tell you I was stressed...I walked out of the canyon parking lot up the road and flagged down a Sheriff, told her what was happening and that I didn't have reception. She said, she doesn't help with these situations and drove off. I was standing their stunned. Not out of entitlement as I'm sure my white skin and blonde hair scream but as a tax payer since I was 14 years old (a hostess as Pei's Manderin was my first job). This b$tch, I thought. Another car came down the road, a tourist family from a whole other country. They stopped to help, tested phones...no one had reception! They offered to drive us to an area that had reception and call for help. My dad in Iowa found a locksmith (could not get enough juice to surf the web but luckily SOS over SMS worked) and luck would have it, we finally got reception, were able to call that locksmith and able to get back in the RV! Very thankful for kind strangers. Law enforcement - do better.

albums.title: Nevada
albums.description: Back in 2004 I visited Las Vegas for the first time - it was a free vacation. A flight that was suppose to be for a boyfriend but they broke up and I went instead. I remember falling in love with the city. The lights, the warmth, the desert landscape, mountains 360 and how much I felt like I belonged. It may sound strange to some, a woman who doesn't drink, smoke or gamble loving Vegas but I did and I always knew one day, I would end up here.

photos.caption: In 2023, I heard that the Bad Waters in Death Valley, the hottest place on the planet, had a lake form for the first time in 10,000 years, I could hardly wait to go see it.
It felt like driving up to a mirage. One of the most incredible views I've ever seen in my entire life.
Can you believe that this is Death Valley and that's overlooking the Bad Waters which is a giant salt basin? Yep, that's before the Lake appeared!

My aunt flew over from Bonita Springs, FL to come stay and take care of me. Surgery after surgery, I've never been more tired of surgeries but when they say Cancer you do whatever it takes. This was one of my after surgery mandatory walks, not a bad view!
Layers on layers of mountains, it's so beautiful! Depending on the day, they change colors, pink, blue to gold, I hope it never gets old.
I don't know if folks are supposed to be out there however, I am a person that minds their own damn business.

Cowboy canyon looking at Red Rock Canyon.

Spent 3 years in the tinest town I've ever been in, Pahrump Nv. Lived on a beautiful golf course with four pools, a club house, gym, golf shop...sort of grandiose for a town of 40,000 people. Didn't golf a day I was there but I did walk up to the gym almost every single day.
My daughter got into an accident and I offered up my Tuscon. My wonderful dad got on a plane, flew to Vegas and got in my car just to drive all the way back to Iowa with me.
The view from the golf course restaurant in Pahrump, Nv.
The golf course that the town treated like a public park haha

Life is meant to be lived! Sold my house in Pahrump, Nv and moved to the City of Henderson! The cityscape, mountains in the backdrop, train tracks all over (reminds me of Cedar Rapids) and the lakes! I am in love with this city.
This is the night I met my first group of friends in Henderson. I was so nervous but they were so welcoming and kind. I am so thankful for them.

albums.description: I love taking photos of those I love: family and dear friends. I have a special place in my heart for portraits because they capture the essence of a person and the relationships we hold dear. These photos are a testament to the beauty of human connection and the stories that unfold through our interactions.

albums.title: Travel
albums.description: Travel has always been a source of inspiration and growth for me. It pushes me beyond my comfort zone, introduces me to new cultures, and lets me see the world through fresh perspectives. These photos capture the spirit of those journeys from breathtaking landscapes to vibrant cityscape and all the small moments of awe that come with exploring somewhere new. My love for travel started with my very first trip as a teenage when my dad took me to Florida for Christmas. Instead of bundling up and navigating snow and freezing temperatures we spent the holiday on a warm beach. One memory we still laugh about is visiting a zoo. I had just started learning sign language and proudly signed “hello” to a chimp. When it raised its hand as if to wave back my dad forever joking the girl that talks to chimps. That trip sparked something in me. From that moment on I knew travel was something I wanted more of in my life. It has continued to bring me joy perspective and inspiration ever since.

albums.title: Albuquerque
albums.description: Warm colors, wide skies, and the quiet hum of the Southwest. I will never forget the cultural shock moving away from Albuquerque, NM to Iowa. I had never been anywhere that was so different from the place I grew up. The desert landscape, the mountains, the sunsets, the culture...I missed it. I will always have a special place in my heart for Albuquerque and the memories I made there. The Christmas luminaries, the hot air balloons, the sandia mountains, the tram, the sunsets...it was all so beautiful and I am so grateful for the time I spent there.

photos.caption: Riding down the tram with my daughter, sister and her son. Honestly, never thought we would all have this moment together. You see, my sister and I spent our early childhood here. Some would say our childhood was less than ideal and we had a lot of trauma. Foster homes, shelters, in and out of our moms house but I focused on the good moments and the good people that were in our lives.
Seeing hundreds of hot air balloons in the sky is a sight to behold. I was lucky enough to see them every year during the Albuquerque International Balloon Fiesta.
My foster parents are raising another generation and I am grateful I got the opportunity to be a part of it. Woke up about 3 am and took em to the balloon fiesta and we had the best time together.
I love the special character balloons have. They are so fun and whimsical and they add a special touch to the balloon fiesta.
Drove up to the Sandia Peak and parked. Sitting in the back of my SUV, watching the sunset and just being was one of the most peaceful moments I've had in a long time.
The sunset riding the tram coming down from the Sandia Peak. I was so grateful to be there with my daughter and sister and her son. It was a moment that I will always cherish.
These tram rides are actually really packed tbh, full of people! But the sunset still draws your focus away from the crowd and towards the beauty of the mountains and the sky.
Tram'n!
Walking around old town with my camera, got a few looks but I was in my own world and I didn't care. I was just trying to capture the beauty of the city and the culture.
